thread.title: Intraday Update: Can the Dow Survive a Tit-for-Tat Trade War? - Barron's

author: Crystal Kim
title: Intraday Update: Can the Dow Survive a Tit-for-Tat Trade War? - Barron's
text:
By Crystal Kim June 15, 2018 1:50 p.m. ET Nothing's immune to the Trump Administration's announcement on Friday that it would slap some $50 billion worth of tariffs on China. The move drew the ire of Beijing, which is expected to retaliate in-kind. Stocks, crude oil, and even safe-haven precious metals took a beating as investors worried about a global trade war disrupting economic growth. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...discuss why fears are overblown;
•...explain why gold has lost its luster;
•...highlight Navistar International's (NAV) 5% rise.
Shock & Awww Stocks are taking a beating on tariffs, but the economy is holding up just fine. Will that be enough to ultimately lift stocks higher?
Consider: Consumer prices are up 2.2% year-over-year, retail sales have surprised to the upside, and despite surging crude oil, U.S. gross domestic product growth appears to be on-track to deliver 4% in the current quarter, says Fundstrat Global Advisors' Tom Lee . And while tariffs are a problem, they're not a big one yet. "We currently believe there is less than a 10% chance of an outright global trade war, but if the risk rises to 20% or more, trade tensions would be more of a risk than a recession," Lee explains.
A scenario where China and the U.S. go tit-for-tat on tariffs could mean potential supply-side disruption, said MKM Partners' chief economist and market strategist Michael Darda . "A negative supply side shock will tend to raise prices and reduce real growth. More restrictive trade and immigration policies thus work against any positive supply side effects from lower corporate tax rates," he wrote in a report published Friday afternoon.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average has tumbled more than 200 points to 24,968, while the S&P 500 has declined 0.4% to 2777.50, and the Nasdaq Composite has dipped .2% to 7744.27.
Meanwhile gold, a safe-haven metal that generally benefits from geopolitical tension, seems to have lost its luster. Gold prices are down more than 2% to about $1,280. Blame it on the Information Age. A more hawkish Fed should've great for gold prices, but the June hike was already priced in. "How aggressive the path is from here likely will have more significant implications," wrote RBC Capital Markets' commodity strategist Christopher Louney .
Once again demonstrating than not everything that glitters is gold. Not even gold itself.
Midday Movers Bunge (BG) is down 2.7% to $68.65 on news that it will delay the initial public offering of its Brazilian unit, citing market conditions.
Finisar (FNSR) reversed early losses and is up 5.1% to $18.61 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The fiber optic component maker earned a nickel a share on revenue of $310.07 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 12 cents a share on revenue of $309.9 million. For the first quarter, it expects to earn between 10 cents and 16 cents a share on revenue of $305 million to $325 million. Consensus calls for EPS of 15 cents on revenue of $316.96 million.
Harley Davidson (HOG) is up 4% to $45.95 after Keybanc Capital Markets suggested that things are looking up near term for the motorcycle maker. Analyst Brett Andress reiterated a Sector Weight rating on the shares, but writes that his research points to "a solid inflection in May domestic retail (up mid-single digits) that is carrying into June, driven by both weather and some nontraditional promos."
LG Display (LPL) is down 7.5% to $9.50 and Universal Display (OLED) is down 7.7% to $91.03 after The Wall Street Journal reported that Apple (AAPL) is looking to use cheaper screens after customer balked at the iPhone X's price tag.
Navistar International (NAV) is up 5.2% to $41.19 on reports that Volkswagen (VLKAY) may be interested in buying the company. — Teresa Rivas
